advances: Finite fixed ownership of whole continuous fiber spaces by actual original cap groups. This test neither selects an optimal ownership nor certifies arbitrary second jets at singular incidence strata.

proof:
The weighted sum of actual margins at $(z,x)$ is $\ell_g(z)$, independent of $x$ by continuous balance and the equalities at the group's source. If this sum is nonnegative at least one margin is nonnegative. For a full-rank circuit of $d+1$ normals the affine map taking $x$ to the vector of its margins has dimension $d$; hence its image is the entire hyperplane of weighted sum $\ell_g(z)$. When $\ell_g(z)<0$ this hyperplane contains the vector with every coordinate equal to $\ell_g(z)$, so the group fails to cover the whole plane.

Below primes denote derivatives at the reference point and sums range over $j\in J_g$. Differentiate the exact equalities for one group:
$$
\begin{aligned}
a_j'\cdot z_g+u_j'\cdot x_g+u_j\cdot x_g'-t_j'&=0,\\
\sum_j \rho_{gj}'&=0,&
\sum_j(\rho_{gj}'u_j+\rho_{gj}u_j')&=0,\\
a_j''\cdot z_g+u_j''\cdot x_g+2u_j'\cdot x_g'+u_j\cdot x_g''-t_j''&=0,\\
\sum_j\rho_{gj}''&=0,&
\sum_j(\rho_{gj}''u_j+2\rho_{gj}'u_j'+\rho_{gj}u_j'')&=0 .
\end{aligned}
$$
Every occurrence uses the same cap jet, so an original shared by several groups imposes all their equations on one tuple. A fixed affine gauge contributes its linear first and second constraints; for a unit normal the two extra equations are $u_j\cdot u_j'=0$ and $u_j\cdot u_j''=-\lVert u_j'\rVert^2$. The projected drift has jets
$$
b_g'=\sum_j(\rho_{gj}'a_j+\rho_{gj}a_j'),\qquad
b_g''=\sum_j(\rho_{gj}''a_j+2\rho_{gj}'a_j'+\rho_{gj}a_j'').
$$
Taylor expansion of each tight row gives the first and second signs, with no restriction from initially slack rows. For prescribed first jets and body/source jets all products of first derivatives are prescribed constants. Thus after selecting the tight rows whose first derivatives are zero, the system in the remaining accelerations is of the form $Aq=a$, $Bq\ge b$. The finite Farkas alternative applies without an independence assumption: infeasibility is equivalent to the existence of $p,r$ with $r\ge0$, $A^{\mathsf T}p+B^{\mathsf T}r=0$, and $a\cdot p+b\cdot r>0$.

For realization, start with the polynomial cap and weight path with the prescribed jets. Along the given actual $C^2$ source path its equality residual is $o(s^2)$ by the first and second equations. Select a fixed invertible minor in the variables, fix the other variables to their trial values, and use the implicit function theorem to solve for this minor along the source path. The inverse derivatives are locally bounded, so the change from the trial variables is $o(s^2)$ and preserves both jets. Each nontrivial tight assigned row now has positive linear or positive quadratic leading term on the positive side, and the strictly slack and identity rows impose no extra condition. Positivity of the finite weights persists; the actual sources remain interior along the stipulated nearby actual body/source path. If a nontrivial row has both displayed coefficients zero, the jets alone do not decide its sign.

statement:
Let $P$ be a finite complete integer base set of a compatible positive-fiber body and fix original nonvertical caps of margins $a_j\cdot z+u_j\cdot x-t_j$. A group $g$ uses indices $J_g$, has interior source $(z_g,x_g)$, and positive weights $\rho_{gj}$ of sum one with $\sum_{j\in J_g}\rho_{gj}u_j=0$; all group margins vanish at its source. Use a single coefficient tuple per original cap. With $b_g=\sum_{j\in J_g}\rho_{gj}a_j$, the group covers the entire plane over each assigned base $z\in Z_g$ if $\ell_g(z)=b_g\cdot(z-z_g)\ge0$. For a full-rank positive circuit of $d+1$ normals this is necessary as well. The fixed assigned sets cover $P$.

For $C^2$ paths with fixed $z_g$ the exact first and second jet equations are those obtained by differentiating the shared through-source, continuous balance, weight normalization and any gauge equations, as displayed in the proof. Each tight assigned row needs $\ell_g'(z)\ge0$ for one-sided feasibility and $\ell_g''(z)\ge0$ if the first derivative vanishes; a two-sided path requires zero tight-row first derivatives. With prescribed body/source jets and fixed cap/weight first jet these second-order conditions are a finite affine feasibility system in the accelerations. If the exact equality map has full row rank in the free cap-chart and weight variables, the body/source path is actual, and each nonidentically-zero tight assigned row has strict first or, when first is zero, strict second slack, the prescribed jets are realized by an actual one-sided path of the cap and weight parameters.
title: Fixed ownership of shared original caps has an exact second-jet test
